Edition: the Paris edition of Études Op. 25 catalogued by NIFC Chopin First Editions Online as 025-1b-LE-009, publisher recorded in the file as Lemoine, Paris (RISM 1001002411, PL-Wbfc 4808/n); encoding Tomasz Sierawski, editing Marta Lawrence and Wojciech Jakubiak-Danek. The performer's edition is not established; first-edition readings can differ from later editions.

Conversion: tools/align/humdrum_convert.py reads the unchanged **kern tokens (Humdrum line timing, spine splits/merges, explicit sounding pitches, ties, graces, tuplets) and writes plain MusicXML for the pinned LilyPond 2.24.4 converter. Dynamics, hairpins, pedalling, fingering, stems, layout comments, *rscale display scaling, cue size and editorial text are not converted; slurs are kept only when both ends lie in one encoded voice. Voices are the encoded Humdrum sub-spines on each staff (MusicXML voices 1-4 upper, 5-8 lower), labelled here only as upper/lower staff.

Source token correction with print reference: 025-1b-LE-009.krn line 269 (bar 21, under 8va) encodes the second staccato octave of the first half-bar as `16edee-'>JJ` / `16dee-`, which contain two pitch names each and are not valid **kern pitches; read as E-flat7/E-flat6 (`16eeee-` / `16eee-`). Print, viewed 19 Oct 2026 in OCVE page images: the French first edition (25-1a-Sm, M. Schlesinger, plate M.S. 2427, p. 32, bar 21; https://chopinonline.ac.uk/ocve/browse/pageview/75382/) and the English first edition (25/7-12-1b-W, Wessel, plate W & Co No. 1833, p. 6, bar 21; https://chopinonline.ac.uk/ocve/browse/pageview/77282/) both engrave this staccato octave one staff step below the preceding accented F-flat octave (encoded `16ffff-X` / `16fff-X`, line 267), with no accidental: E, flat by the G-flat-major key signature. The encoding's other half-bars of the sequence step down the same way (lines 273/275 C-flat7/C-flat6 then B-flat6/B-flat5; 280/282 E-double-flat7 then D-flat7; 286/288 B-double-flat6 then A-flat6). Verovio 6.3.0 reads the malformed tokens as E and D. The downloaded bytes are unchanged; the correction is applied in memory and retained in the check report.
Recording: Edward Neeman, piano, c. 2014 (Musopen; content/listen module). The tuning estimate is +4 cents (441.02 Hz); no transposition.

ties.basis: 025-1b-LE-009.krn lines 486/489: source tie continues in another encoded voice of the same staff; LilyPond cannot tie across voices, so the note is held, not reattacked.

endpointMeasurements.label: first
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features (dB re the 95th-percentile total). First: the opening G-flat3/B-flat4 (q0) is the first sound; total energy is -47 to -36 dB before 0.75 s, and the A-sharp4 band rises -42 -> -14 dB and F-sharp3 -47 -> -30 dB at 0.80-0.90 s (primary onset 0.882 s), followed by B-flat5/G-flat5 at 1.0-1.06 s and C-flat5/C-flat6 at 1.18-1.22 s. The broad 0-4 s first-pass window chose 2.74 s, two bars in, and compressed bar 1. Last: the final staccato G-flat chord (q100: G-flat2/G-flat3/B-flat3/G-flat4) rises at 65.55-65.65 s (F-sharp4 -38 -> -22 dB, F-sharp3 -34 -> -21 dB, F-sharp2 -47 -> -40 dB; adaptive onset 65.643 s), after B-flat3 64.5, G-flat4 64.7, C-flat5/E-flat4 64.9 and B-flat4/D-flat4 65.15 s; the primary detector has no onset there (nearest 65.178 s), so the last-anchor disagreement is about 0.41 s. The broad 50-68 s window chose 61.03 s, which squeezed bars 48-51 into 0.6 s; the recording decays to below -45 dB by about 66.8 s.

endpointMeasurements.label: bar-37-C-flat4-A-flat4
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features: after the bar-36 ritenuto the bar-37 chord (q72) rises at 47.70 s and is held; the G-flat2 eighth (q72.5) begins a slow F-sharp2/F-sharp3 rise from 48.35 s (primary onset 48.402 s). The next group, C-flat4/D-flat3 with A-flat4 (q73), rises at 48.95-49.00 s (B3 band -40 -> -22 dB, detector edge 48.96 s, primary onset 48.982 s), and the a-tempo sixteenths follow every 0.15-0.18 s (D-flat5/A-flat5 49.12-49.16, B-flat 49.30, C-flat 49.45, bar 38 D-flat5 49.65 s). The unconstrained map placed q73 at 48.364 s and q73.25 at 48.525 s, about 0.6 s early, then stalled 0.76 s before q73.5.

endpointMeasurements.label: bar-49-G-flat-chord
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS, cached pitch features: the bar-49 downbeat (G-flat1/G-flat2 with the G-flat6/B-flat5 close of the right-hand run, q96) follows the last bar-48 sixteenth (primary onset 62.613 s); A-sharp5/F-sharp6 rise -36 -> -19 dB and F-sharp2 -32 -> -27 dB at 62.70-62.80 s (detector edge 62.74 s, primary onset 62.798 s). The unconstrained map placed it at 62.912 s and fitted bars 48-50 with an almost straight path (62-65.4 s), 0.1-0.3 s late.

endpointMeasurements.label: bar-50-G-flat-octave
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS: the bar-50 left-hand G-flat1/G-flat2 octave (q98) after the D-flat octaves; the summed G-flat band rises at 63.86-63.96 s (detector edge 63.86 s; primary onset 63.901 s). Unconstrained: 64.141 s.

endpointMeasurements.label: bar-50-B-flat3
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS: q99, the right hand's B-flat3 (A-sharp3 band -34 -> -23 dB at 64.45-64.55 s) with the G-flat octave; detector edge 64.46 s, primary onset 64.540 s. Unconstrained: 64.786 s.

endpointMeasurements.label: bar-50-C-flat5-E-flat4
endpointMeasurements.basis: MEAS: q99.5, C-flat5/E-flat4 over the D-flat octave; the C-flat5 (B4) band rises -25 -> -10 dB and E-flat4 -24 -> -14 dB at 64.85-64.95 s; detector edge 64.88 s, primary onset 64.923 s. Unconstrained: 65.108 s. The following B-flat4/D-flat4 (q99.75) rises at 65.10-65.20 s and the final chord at 65.55-65.65 s.
